title: Obesity, morbid obesity and BMI
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's weight diagnosis and BMI, if reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint
Weight management and follow-up.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old woman presenting today for a scheduled follow-up regarding her weight. She reports that she has been attempting to incorporate more movement into her daily routine but finds it challenging due to joint stiffness. She expresses a desire to lose weight to improve her overall mobility and comfort. She denies any acute shortness of breath or chest pain today.

Medication List
Multivitamin daily.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. She appears in no acute distress. Vital signs are stable, with a BMI of 32.7. Physical examination reveals a well-nourished female with no acute inflammatory signs.

Assessment
1. Obesity.

Plan
We discussed the patient's current weight status and the goals for management. I provided comprehensive counseling regarding a balanced diet, emphasizing portion control and increased fiber intake. We also discussed a gradual activity plan, including short walks around the house to improve cardiovascular health. She will return in three months for a follow-up weight check.

Electronically signed, P. O'Brien, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Obesity documented by the provider: E66.9. The coder does not upgrade it to morbid obesity from the BMI.
BMI 32.x with a provider weight diagnosis: add Z68.32.

distractors.why: Only the provider can diagnose morbid obesity; the BMI does not change the diagnosis.
The BMI is documented and the provider diagnosed the weight condition: add the Z68 code.
